Do you believe in God, a God, or a higher power that could explain how we all ended up here on the only known planet, to us, that is hospitable?

But seriously, and more complicatedly, I think that the concept that humans have developed about a higher power is a method with which we deal with a concept that we cannot fully grasp. I believe there is an aspect to the universe that can only be defined by the infinite.

It is suspected that the universe exists in a form of expansion and contraction, and that the big bang may be a side effect of the collapse and compaction of the last universe, and that this cycle may be repetitive in nature. Meaning that although the life of the current universe can be measured, the life of that which drives the creation of the universe currently cannot.

The other observation that drives me toward this conclusion is scientific progress. It is an amazing paradox that as scientific knowledge increases, and the number of things that we "understand" increases, the number of things that we discover that either contradict that which we used to "know" and the number of things that we discover that we do not yet understand increase at a much more rapid pace. That is to say, that as we learn, we learn more about what we do not know than what we do know. If that patterns increases, as I assume it would with the entire universe to explore, the concept of strings and parallel universes and quantum physics, among a plethora of other mind boggling scientific concepts, the ratio of what we know to what we don't will continue to increase.

The fact that all of this exists points me at something that must underlie the whole experience of being. Now, that's not (to me) some bearded guy sitting on a cloud somewhere, but rather an energy/flow/connection, something so complicated and enormous that the only way that the human mind could grasp it would be to boil it down into its most simple form, an all-powerful deity.

TL;DR - The universe is so complex, there is so much that we don't understand, and the amount we do not understand increases at a pace far greater than that which we do understand, there must be something underneath it all, and humans being as simple as we are, needed some concept which we could grasp, discuss and teach, thus we created and named a concept, "God", "Allah", whatever.

But this is only one simple human's take.

EDIT: Spacing...

The universe is so complex, there is so much that we don't understand, and the amount we do not understand increases at a pace far greater than that which we do understand, there must be something underneath it all,

Why must there be something underneath it all?

Perhaps I left "underneath it all" a little too vague. What I am saying is that every discovery has led to further questions about the makeup of the thing being investigated. We cracked the atom to find individual particles, we cracked the particles to find sub atomic particles, and now we are in the process of trying to crack those sub atomic particles to determine what they are made of. There is something fundamentally similar about the composition of the universe and the composition of the smallest particles, and that similarity speaks to some sort of relationship, and even if we cannot categorize that relationship, we cannot ignore that it exists, and we need to have some way of discussing it. Whether you call it intelligent design, God, energy or even coincidence, it is there.

One of the things that I like to consider is the concept of the 10 dimensions that currently are proposed. At the core of it, for me, is the fact that at any point I exist in a sort of existential cloud that consists of every possibility for every decision that I have ever made or will ever make or have ever or will ever be affected by from the beginning of time to the end of time. That cloud is massive, infinity cubed kind of massive, and I am that cloud, but I am also a single point in that cloud. So when I die, does the cloud die? Do I jump to some other position in the cloud? Am I defined by the cloud or am I defined by the point that I currently occupy right now? It seriously boggles the mind.

To exist in a universe that enormous, in an "existence cloud" that incomprehensibly massive, and ignore the possibility that there is some shared thing between me, my cloud, you, your cloud and everyone else is very arrogant on my part. I have the ability to realize how little we know about existence, but I am quick to deny any possibility? I have the knowledge to deny that there may, in fact, be a common thread that connects everything in existence at some level we have not even dreamed of investigating yet? I know for a fact that I do not, and I would encourage others to examine why they believe they do.

In my opinion, the question is not how we inexplicably ended up on the one inhabitable planet in the big space around us. I like to approach this from the other side.

In a vast universe with billions of galaxies, and billion billions of stars, and billion billion billons of planets, there will be quite a number of planets that have conditions suitable for some form of life. Of these planets, some will generate carbon-based molecules through atmospheric processes and compounds on the surface. An even smaller amount of planets will develop some kind of reproducing organisms from these carbon-based molecules.
